title: Likes, wants and plans
can: Say what you like and what you fancy, and make plans for the weekend.
doneText: You can now say what you like, suggest something and make plans with ir a.

discover.intro: All six sentences mean "I like…". Spot why the verb changes between blue and orange.
discover.question: Why gusta in blue but gustan in orange?
options: The verb agrees with the thing you like: one thing or an action takes gusta, plural things take gustan.
Gustan means you like it a lot.
Gustan is for animals and people, gusta for objects.
discover.nudge: Not quite. Look at what comes after the verb: el café and bailar against los gatos and las tapas.
discover.reveal: Gustar works back to front. "Me gusta el café" is literally "coffee pleases me", so the verb agrees with the coffee, not with you. Me, te, le show who does the liking:

hooks.title: Plans: ir a + verb
rows: They're going to stay at home.

learn.title: Want, go and fancy
learn.sub: Tap any row to hear it

blocks.text: Querer is a boot verb like tener: quiero, quieres, quiere, but queremos and queréis. Add a verb for what you want to do: quiero ver la Alhambra.
Apetecer is very Spain: ¿Te apetece un café? (Do you fancy a coffee?). It works like gustar: me apetece, te apetece, nos apetece.

blocks.title: Me gusta or quiero
blocks.note: Gustar is for what you like in general. Querer and apetecer are for what you want or fancy right now.

blocks.text: Never say "yo gusto" for "I like": it means "I am pleasing". It's always me gusta.

To name the person who likes something, put a in front and keep the le: a mi hermana le gustan los perros (my sister likes dogs), a Pedro le gusta el café. For yourself, a mí me gusta stresses the I: I like it (even if you don't).

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Message a friend: say two things you like (one with gusta, one with gustan) and suggest a plan for the weekend with ir a.
write.starter: Me gusta…  Me gustan…  El sábado vamos a…
write.model: Me gusta mucho bailar y me gustan las tapas. ¿Te apetece salir el sábado? Vamos a ir de tapas por La Latina.
checklist: Gusta for one thing or an action, gustan for plural things
Plans: voy a or vamos a + verb

boss.title: Weekend plans in Granada
boss.persona: You are Nuria, a friendly woman from Granada the learner met at a language exchange. You chat about likes, dislikes and plans for the weekend, and suggest things to do in Granada: the Alhambra, free tapas, flamenco, the Albaicín. Use tú.

turns.en: Hi! Hey, do you like flamenco?
choices: ¡Sí, me encanta!
¡Sí, yo gusto mucho!
"Yo gusto" means "I am pleasing". Say me gusta or me encanta.
¡Sí, me gustan mucho!
El flamenco is one thing: me gusta.

turns.en: Great! What are you going to do on Saturday?
choices: Voy a visitar la Alhambra.
Voy visitar la Alhambra.
Plans need the a: voy a visitar.
Vas a visitar la Alhambra.
Vas a is "you're going to". About yourself: voy a.

turns.npc: ¡Qué bien! ¿Y te apetece ir a un tablao por la noche?
turns.en: How nice! And do you fancy going to a flamenco show in the evening?
choices: Sí, me apetece mucho.
Sí, apetezco mucho.
Apetecer works like gustar: me apetece.
Sí, te apetece mucho.
Te apetece is "you fancy". About yourself: me apetece.

turns.npc: Perfecto. ¿Quieres cenar antes? Hay unas tapas muy buenas en el Albaicín.
turns.en: Perfect. Do you want to have dinner first? There are some very good tapas in the Albaicín.
choices: Sí, quiero probar las tapas de Granada.
Sí, quero probar las tapas de Granada.
Querer is a boot verb: quiero.
Sí, me gustan probar las tapas de Granada.
An action takes gusta, not gustan. But here you want it now: quiero probar.

boss.closing: ¡Hecho! Quedamos el sábado a las ocho en la Plaza Nueva.
boss.closingEn: Done! Let's meet on Saturday at eight in Plaza Nueva.
boss.chatOpening: ¿Y qué más te gusta hacer cuando viajas?
boss.chatOpeningEn: And what else do you like doing when you travel?
